unit.why: The division is an anthology of ethical and kabbalistic teachings on burial, gazing, eating, faith and speaking Torah, quoted from Hasidic books. It contains only three very short anecdotes used as exempla inside the teachings.
unit.boundary_note: Continues the topical anthology of the previous division and goes on into the next one (מענין אמירת תורה continues). The anecdotes are embedded exempla, not standalone stories.

stories.start_quote: ששמעתי מהחסיד הצדיק מו״ה וישא זללה"ה
stories.end_quote: לא בשביל הנאתו והוא מדרגה גדולה
stories.summary_en: The pious R. Yisa fasted three days because he had said the blessing over bread for his own pleasure, to still his hunger, rather than for God's sake.

stories.summary_en: Fleeing the Ishmaelites, the Besht spread his belt on the wide Dniester and crossed it by pure faith, without any holy name.

stories.summary_en: An unlearned man asked the Maggid of Mezritch for words of Torah. He clung only to the odd-seeming reading of שמרה as 'dregs' and missed its moral lesson.
